capabilityGroups.title: Tool execution duration across agent core, application Session, TUI and durable Harness
capabilityGroups.rationale: One frozen contract (monotonic execute-only durationMs) with four distinct owners/consumers; the rows stay separate because each consumer is migrated by a different owner slice, but they share one comparison family.

capabilityGroups.title: Native extension registration, hooks, wrapping and run triggering
capabilityGroups.rationale: The same selected native extension contract appears as an application Session seam (1049/1051) and as a durable Harness seam (1056). Owners and consumers differ, so rows stay separate; the group records one membership authority and one removal of the historical ADR 0066 clause.

capabilityGroups.title: Tool selection modifiers and resumed loadout
capabilityGroups.rationale: Application Session resume rows and product CLI/session behavior; one contract, application owner only.

capabilityGroups.title: Durable task semantics seen through tasks (1055) and Harness workflows (1056)
capabilityGroups.rationale: Both lanes drive the same Harness.open entrypoint with different scenario slices: 1055 exercises task/submission scheduling, versioning, ownership and crash recovery; 1056 exercises the workflow, registry, compaction, hooks and inspect/observability slices. Same owner (cch_durable); the rows stay separate and cross-reference instead of duplicating or hiding evidence.

capabilityGroups.title: Durable-required Chord contracts (1054 overview rows, 1057 detail rows, 1056 durable usage rows)
capabilityGroups.rationale: 1054 records five coarse Chord rows the durable session depends on; 1057 records the same contracts per operation; 1056 records durable's own usage. One owner (cch_chord), one consumer (cch_durable); 1054 rows are the coarse view of 1057 detail and are kept with an explicit overlap resolution rather than deleted.

capabilityGroups.title: Codemode core contracts (1053) and durable/application integration (1053/1056)
capabilityGroups.rationale: The reusable VM/declaration/Remote contract belongs to cch_codemode; the application catalog, store, loadout and durable script integrations are consumers. Rows stay separate per owner; the group records the true contract identity behind the similar names.

capabilityGroups.title: TUI toolkit exports (1050) and Native TUI product consumers (1051)
capabilityGroups.rationale: The toolkit contract belongs to cch_tui; the product TUI behavior belongs to cch_coding_agent (frontend_tui). The toolkit rows for a component and the product rows that consume it are adjacent but not the same contract; the group keeps the toolkit/product split explicit, and the overlap resolution beside it names the three adjacent 1051 rows and promotes none of the seven product rows.

capabilityGroups.title: Application Session transcript (1048) versus durable Session/storage (1054)
capabilityGroups.rationale: Two distinct runtimes with different storage formats and consumers. ADR 0075 keeps the ordinary application Session separate from durable; no row merges and no consumer may cross the boundary.

overlapResolutions.resolution: The toolkit export contract is cch_tui; the Native TUI product behavior is cch_coding_agent's frontend_tui implementation target. The seven 1050 product-entry rows stay not-audited/unverified for v1.3.0 and are not counted as verified by any 1051 capture. #1051 holds three adjacent capability rows in the same product area (mode-switch-renderer, exit-restoration, hardware-cursor); only two product rows name a counterpart, and a counterpart is adjacent, not equal: neither 1051 row observes the 1050 setting and neither is verified. The other five rows have no 1051 row at all. Every row keeps its own visible missing-observation statement.

no #1051 row covers the --tui-mode CLI flag; the frozen v1.3.0 behavior of this product entry has no observation

overlapResolutions.resolution: Application Session transcript (JSONL session files, coding-agent owner) and durable Session (transactional document/entry/storage contract, durable owner) are different runtimes. The legacy SQLite SessionStore row stays no-decision and is the coupling to split; it is not durable's storage and not the application's final transcript format.

Both lanes drive the same Harness.open entrypoint with different scenario slices: 1055 exercises task/submission scheduling, versioning, ownership and crash recovery, while 1056 exercises the workflow, registry, compaction, hooks and inspect/observability slices. Same owner (cch_durable); rows stay separate and cross-referenced, with no duplicate merge and no hidden coverage.

Chord Context/documents/delta are document-tracking semantics owned by cch_chord and consumed only by cch_durable. Codemode context/globals/store are script-VM semantics owned by cch_codemode (with application and durable integrations). Similar names do not merge: the true contract identity is the owner plus the frozen source family.

Native extension registration/hooks/run triggering is one selected membership with an application Session consumer (1049/1051) and a durable Harness consumer (1056). The historical ADR 0066 #865 tool-source clause does not reopen this; direct third-party TS/JS execution stays excluded.

Generic MCP client/transports/OAuth stay in cch_mcp; application config, persistence, exposure, management UI, session-tool binding and codemode's MCP refresh stay in cch_coding_agent. The codemode-mcp-refresh row is an application integration, not an MCP protocol contract.

retainedLimitations.statement: #1052 application observations use the public createMcpExtension factory with a minimal public ExtensionAPI/ExtensionContext host stub, not a full AgentSession or real management UI; later Session/Interactive comparisons are required.
#1053 application-catalog observations use public createCodemodeExtension/createCodemodeDescription/toCodemodeDeclaration with a minimal ExtensionAPI host stub, not a full AgentSession or real TUI.

The original audits did not run C++ comparisons. Later slices do have comparison tests and reports; only a complete validated record in 1058-deliveries.json promotes a whole row. The source audit verification states remain historical provenance.
#1047 records frozen symbol names without file paths; the consolidated frozenSymbols stay verbatim and the C++ targets were corrected from the merger review.

The original audit used mismatched thinkingLevelMap fixtures. The refreshed #810 implementation slice is now closed; its evidence and comparison boundary are retained without automatically promoting the capability row.
Crash evidence is real SIGKILL and SQLite reopen with a live OS page cache; power loss, fsync failure and multi-process concurrency are not proven.
Pi-only JSONL/SQLite reopen is captured; both C++ interchange directions and alternating writers remain unverified.

The original audit lacked raw PTY evidence. #1123 and #1125 now record actual protocol/lifecycle PTY comparisons. Actual emulator rendering and image/cursor/clipboard outcomes remain unverified where dated emulator evidence is missing; see 1124-dated-terminal-evidence.md.

The original audit recorded a post-Enter model-selector assertion failure (17 passed / 1 failed). The refreshed #808 implementation slice is closed with a dated PTY record in 808-model-selector-pty-2026-10-22.md; the old failure is historical evidence, not a current known failure.
Serial registry registration proves bundle integrity only; it never makes a row C++-verified.
